cards.explanation: The answer is loves. Moses says to the LORD, "Surely You love the people…" (Deuteronomy 33:3). Flaming fire and holy ones in one verse, and the next thing out of his mouth is love. I think that's a pretty tender turn, friends.

The answer is law. Moses says each one receives His words, "…the law that Moses gave us, the possession of the assembly of Jacob." (Deuteronomy 33:4). A possession is something you hold on to. I think Moses is saying the whole assembly of Jacob owns this law, like a family guarding the one cookie recipe nobody is allowed to lose.

The answer is True. Moses says, "So the LORD became King in Jeshurun when the leaders of the people gathered, when the tribes of Israel came together." (Deuteronomy 33:5). Jeshurun is a name used here for Israel. The tribes gathered, friends, and the LORD is King over them.

The answer is False. Moses says, "Let Reuben live and not die, nor his men be few." (Deuteronomy 33:6). He's asking that Reuben's men not be few. One verse for Reuben, friends, and it's all about staying alive and staying counted.

The answer is True. Moses says, "With his own hands he defends his cause, but may You be a help against his foes." (Deuteronomy 33:7). Judah does his part with his own hands. Moses still asks the LORD to be a help against his foes.
The answer is Massah and Meribah. Moses says the LORD tested Levi "at Massah" and contested him "…at the waters of Meribah." (Deuteronomy 33:8). Those are the two places Moses names, friends.

The answer is that he kept God's word and covenant. Moses says Levi did all that "…for he kept Your word and maintained Your covenant." (Deuteronomy 33:9). The text gives the reason, so we don't have to guess. Levi held on to God's word through all of it.
The answer is True. Moses says, "He will teach Your ordinances to Jacob and Your law to Israel…" (Deuteronomy 33:10). Levi gets a teaching job for the whole people, friends. That's a big job.

The answer is upon His shoulders. Moses says, "God shields him all day long, and upon His shoulders he rests." (Deuteronomy 33:12). Benjamin is called the beloved of the LORD. That's a picture of resting while someone else carries the weight.

The answer is the One who dwelt in the burning bush. Moses asks for "…the favor of Him who dwelt in the burning bush." to rest on the head of Joseph. (Deuteronomy 33:16). Moses is asking for that favor on top of the dew, the harvest and the mountains. The blessing for Joseph has a lot of layers, friends.

The answer is Ephraim and Manasseh. Moses says, "Such are the myriads of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh." (Deuteronomy 33:17). Those are Joseph's two sons (Genesis 41:51-52). Their names close out his blessing, friends.

The answer is sacrifices of righteousness. Moses says of Zebulun and Issachar, "They will call the peoples to a mountain; there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness." (Deuteronomy 33:19). One tribe is told to rejoice in journeys and the other in tents. Both end up calling the peoples to the same mountain.

The answer is True. Moses says, "For they will feast on the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand." (Deuteronomy 33:19). A feast from the sea and from the sand, friends. That's a lot of abundance.
The answer is a lion. Moses says of Gad, "He lies down like a lion…" (Deuteronomy 33:20). Gad is pictured as a strong, fierce one. That's one big cat to compare a tribe to, friends.

The answer is the LORD's justice and ordinances. Moses says Gad "…administered the LORD’s justice and His ordinances for Israel." (Deuteronomy 33:21). Gad came with the leaders of the people, and that's what Gad carried out.
The answer is Bashan. Moses says, "Dan is a lion’s cub, leaping out of Bashan." (Deuteronomy 33:22). Short blessing, big leap, friends. That's one verse and a whole lot of motion.

The answer is False. Moses says of Naphtali, "he shall take possession of the sea and the south." (Deuteronomy 33:23). So it's the sea and the south, not mountains and the north. Swapping two words can really change a map, friends.
The answer is to be the most blessed of sons. Moses says, "May Asher be the most blessed of sons…" (Deuteronomy 33:24). He aims high for the last tribe on the list, friends. And he's not done yet.

The answer is enemy. Moses says, "He drives out the enemy before you…" (Deuteronomy 33:27). That comes right after the eternal God is their dwelling place and the everlasting arms are underneath. Solid ground below and the enemy driven out ahead, friends.

The answer is securely. Moses says, "So Israel dwells securely…" (Deuteronomy 33:28). The land has grain and new wine, and even the heavens drip with dew. I think that's a pretty peaceful picture of home, friends.

The answer is a people saved by the LORD. Moses asks, "Blessed are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD?" (Deuteronomy 33:29). Saved is the word he puts on Israel, friends. Then he keeps going and calls the LORD their shield and sword.

The answer is True. Moses says, "He is the shield that protects you, the sword in which you boast." (Deuteronomy 33:29). The LORD is both the shield and the sword, friends. That's the whole defense and offense in one.
